title: Backend entry scenario counter race condition
topic: Backend entry scenario counter race condition
question: You built a 'view count' feature: each page view runs 'read the current count, add 1, save it back'. Under heavy traffic, the count ends up lower than the actual number of views. Why, and how would you fix it?
idealAnswer:
Identifies the lost update problem: two requests can both read the same starting count before either writes back, so one increment gets silently overwritten by the other

Explains this gets worse under concurrency/load precisely because more requests overlap in that read-modify-write window

Proposes an atomic update as the fix, e.g. UPDATE counts SET count = count + 1 WHERE id = ..., which lets the database do the increment in one step instead of round-tripping through the application

Recognizes this is a general pattern (read-modify-write without atomicity), not a one-off bug, and that the fix is to push the operation into the database rather than trying to synchronize application code

Bonus: mentions alternatives like a database-level increment counter, or an atomic increment in something like Redis if the counter doesn't need to live in the primary database
